rail.title: Apps
rail.emptyHint: Play sound in an app, then refresh
rail.alsoHint: Apply the same change to this app
rail.stopRoute: Stop output and return to the system default
rail.stopAllConfirm: Click again to return everything to the system default

sourceLevel.valueLabel: Level this app gives the audio of {{process}}, in percent
sourceLevel.hint: Gain this app applies to this program's audio on its way to the devices it is duplicated to, as a percentage: 100 leaves it as produced, below attenuates, above amplifies. Like the device volume and the delay, it acts on the duplicated copies only — the device Windows plays directly is not affected. Drag sideways, or scroll / use the arrow keys for {{step}}% at a time (hold Shift for ×10); click to type an exact value

deviceLatency.reading: Measured here: {{ms}} ms. Covers the software side only — what a codec or a Bluetooth link adds on top cannot be observed from user mode

deviceVolume.valueLabel: Volume of {{device}}, relative to the loudest device, in percent

stage.guide: Select an app on the left
stage.promoteTitle: Make this the device the system plays directly; the others become copies of it
stage.promoteBlockedTitle: Its delay compensation is larger than the Main device's, and the system plays that one directly — software delay can only hold sound back, so this device can only align as a copy

dock.preview: The sound of {{process}} will play through {{device}}
dock.previewMany: The sound of {{n}} apps will play through {{device}}
dock.guide: Pick where this app should play

settings.title: Settings
settings.glassLiteDesc: Skips the frosted refraction and the pointer-tracked highlight, so panes turn solid and weak GPUs stay cool. Windows with transparency effects turned off starts here automatically.
settings.autoRememberDesc: Remember each program's device routing and restore it automatically
settings.resetEndpointsDesc: Releases a program that no longer follows the system's playback device; routed programs are left alone
settings.stopAllRoutesDesc: Returns every routed program to the system default at once. The programs a route is not using are left alone.
settings.closeToTrayDesc: When on, closing hides the window to the tray while routes keep running; when off, closing quits the app and stops them
settings.autostartDesc: Launches silently into the tray at sign-in; remembered routes are ready before you open anything
settings.delayNote: Delay is set per device: here, on the settings rows, or with the − / + under a copy on the stage. It applies only when one program goes to several devices — a single-device route is played by the system directly.
settings.calibrationNote: The measured latency covers the software side only; what a Bluetooth link itself adds cannot be measured here, so align by ear.
settings.delayRangeDesc: Delays can be set within this ± range
settings.delayStepDesc: How much each − / + click changes; an exact value can also be typed
settings.sourceLevelsAlignDesc: Brings every duplicating program that is playing up to the loudest one's level
settings.sourceLevelsNote: A program playing through several devices wears its level as the dial beside the hub at the centre of the stage. The level is the gain this app applies to its own copy of that sound — the program's own volume and anything Windows stores are untouched. 100 leaves it as produced, and it acts on the copies only.
settings.aboutDesc: Per-app audio routing for Windows — Rust talking to Windows Core Audio directly, no third-party executables.

startup.upgradeTitle: An earlier version ran on this PC
startup.upgradeBody: It may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you encounter this, clear it with the button below; otherwise no action is needed.
startup.upgradeBodyVersion: The last version to run on this PC was {{version}}, and it may have left some programs fixed to one output device: they no longer follow the device you switch to in Windows, and a reboot does not bring them back. If you encounter this, clear it with the button below; otherwise no action is needed.
startup.resetHint: This clears every program that is running now, including a device you set by hand in the volume mixer. A program that is not running keeps its device until it starts.
startup.resetDone: Cleared the fixed output device of {{n}} program(s).
startup.resetRemaining: {{processes}} could not be cleared — a program must be playing audio to be released; try again.
startup.firstRunBody: Select an app on the left, choose an output device, then press Apply — nothing changes until you do. Select further devices to play through all of them at once. If a program ever stops following the device you switch to in Windows, the per-app output reset in Settings releases it.
